name: vegetable korma
instructions:
North indian vegetable curry with a CASHEW-and-TOMATO base and a mix of chunky vegetables playing the meat role. Onion and garlic get FOOD-PROCESSED into a puree first (same technique as chole-masala's onion treatment) so they disappear into the sauce; the chunky vegetables (carrots, potatoes, peas, green beans, cauliflower) become the visible / textural components — the 'meat' of the dish. UNTESTED so far — first draft.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

BASE (pureed):
- 1 large RED ONION, pureed
- 4-5 cloves GARLIC, added to the puree
- 1/2 to 3/4 cup CASHEWS (soaked 30 min in hot water first, then blended smooth with a splash of water)

AROMATICS / SPICES (basic north indian stack):
- 2 tbsp ghee (or vegetable oil)
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tsp cumin (whole, bloomed in the ghee)
- 1 tbsp fresh GINGER, grated
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1/2 to 1 tsp turmeric
- 1 tsp garam masala
- 1 tsp kashmiri chili powder
- salt to taste

TOMATO:
- 2-3 fresh TOMATOES, chopped OR 1 can crushed tomatoes
- 1-2 tbsp TOMATO PASTE (for depth)

CHUNKY VEGETABLES (the 'meat'):
- 2 medium POTATOES, cubed
- 2 CARROTS, coarse chopped
- 1 cup GREEN BEANS, cut into bite-sized pieces
- 1 small head CAULIFLOWER, broken into florets
- 1 cup PEAS (frozen, no need to thaw)

FINISH:
- fresh cilantro, chopped
- kasoori methi (crumbled in off heat — see notes)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. SOAK CASHEWS: cover cashews with hot water; let sit 30 min. Then blend smooth with a splash of the soaking water. Set aside.
2. PUREE ONION + GARLIC: food-process the red onion and garlic together into a smooth puree (see notes on why pureed).
3. BLOOM WHOLE SPICES: heat ghee in a heavy pot. Add the bay leaf and whole cumin; bloom 30 sec until fragrant.
4. COOK THE ONION PUREE: add the pureed onion + garlic. Cook 10-15 min on medium, stirring, until the puree darkens and the raw-onion smell is gone. Add the grated ginger; cook 1 min more.
5. ADD GROUND SPICES: stir in coriander, turmeric, garam masala, kashmiri chili powder, salt. Toast in the fat 30 sec.
6. ADD TOMATO: stir in the chopped/canned tomatoes + tomato paste. Cook 8-10 min until the mixture thickens and the fat starts to separate.
7. ADD CASHEW CREAM: stir the blended cashew cream into the base. Simmer 2-3 min to integrate.
8. ADD CHUNKY VEGETABLES: add potatoes, carrots, green beans, cauliflower. Add water as needed to just cover. Simmer covered 20-25 min until the vegetables are tender.
9. ADD PEAS: stir in the frozen peas near the end (5 min before serving) — they only need to warm through, not cook down.
10. FINISH: scatter chopped cilantro and crumbled kasoori methi off heat. Taste for salt.
notes:
First draft — untested. Log the first cook when it happens.

=== PUREED ONION + GARLIC BASE — SAME TECHNIQUE AS CHOLE ===

Onion and garlic get FOOD-PROCESSED into a smooth puree before they hit the pan. Reason: this puts the aromatics into the sauce structure itself, leaving the chunky vegetables (potatoes, carrots, green beans, cauliflower, peas) to be the visible / textural components — the 'meat' of the dish. If you leave the onions chunky, they compete with the vegetables for textural attention and the dish reads as a chunky-everything mess without a clear protein-slot analog.

Same technique as chole-masala (which pre-boils then purees the onions for the same reason). Different from mediterranean-dal and himachali-chana-madra, both of which use finely diced or chunky onions.

UNLIKE CHOLE — NO NEED TO PRE-BOIL: chole boils the onions first because pureeing raw onions is bitter. Here it's less critical because the onion puree cooks down for 10-15 min in ghee, which softens any raw edge. If you want to be safe, a 2-3 min pre-boil doesn't hurt.

=== VEGETABLES-AS-MEAT — ROLE REVERSAL ===

The chunky vegetables (potatoes, carrots, green beans, cauliflower, peas) collectively play the meat role in this dish. Same role-reversal principle as mediterranean-dal (where dal is the sauce and diced vegetables are the meat) — here the cashew-and-tomato base is the sauce, and the chunky vegetable mix is the meat.

Which means: don't skimp on any single vegetable and don't add so much that the sauce can't coat them. The vegetables should be visible and distinct in the finished dish; the sauce should cling but not drown them.

=== CASHEW CREAM — CANONICAL KORMA MOVE ===

Soaked-and-blended cashews are what makes korma korma. The cashew cream folded into the tomato base is what gives the sauce its signature creamy-nutty body. Soak 30 min in hot water first so the cashews blend smooth; blending dry or under-soaked cashews leaves gritty bits in the sauce.

QUANTITY: 1/2 cup for a lighter sauce; up to 3/4 cup for a richer one. Depends on how much sauce body you want against the vegetable load.

=== BASIC NORTH INDIAN SPICE STACK ===

What's in the primary list: bay leaf, whole cumin, ginger, ground coriander, turmeric, garam masala, kashmiri chili powder. That's the basic stack — no cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, or asafetida.

CLASSICAL KORMA WHOLE-SPICE ADDITIONS (SECONDARY, WORTH TRYING): traditional korma often blooms cardamom pods, cloves, and cinnamon with the bay leaf and cumin at the start. All three are secondary here — welcome additions when you want to lean more classical-korma. Chana-masala's clashing list flags these, but korma is a different register and takes them fine.

KASOORI METHI (OFF HEAT): crumbled in at the finish alongside the cilantro. Load-bearing indian herbal note; same role as in the chickpea family (chole, chana masala, mediterranean-dal, rajma).

=== VEGETABLE-SPECIFIC NOTES ===

POTATOES: cubed, add early — they take the longest to cook through. Standard indian potato in curry.
CARROTS: coarse-chopped, add with the potatoes.
GREEN BEANS: bite-sized pieces, add with the potatoes/carrots. Will cook down more than the harder vegetables — that's fine, they melt into the sauce.
CAULIFLOWER: florets, add with the harder vegetables. Cauliflower absorbs the sauce well; don't over-simmer or they fall apart.
PEAS: FROZEN, added at the END (last 5 min) — they only need to warm through. Adding early turns them into mush.

=== VEGAN — DAIRY-FREE BY DEFAULT ===

This recipe as written is vegan (ghee is optional; vegetable oil works). Traditional korma often uses yogurt or heavy cream alongside the cashew cream; both would work here as secondaries for a richer dish, but the cashew cream carries the body on its own without them.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- chole-masala: same pureed-onion-base technique. Different flavor register (dark tea + cardamom + cloves + cinnamon vs cashew + tomato + basic north indian spices).
- chana-masala: chickpea sibling. Simpler; no cashew cream, no chunky vegetable mix.
- mediterranean-dal: vegetables-as-meat role reversal parallel (dal as sauce, vegetables as meat). Different sauce structure (lentils vs cashew cream).
- himachali-chana-madra: another cashew-adjacent (uses soaked almonds not cashews) north indian curry. Different substrate (cottage cheese / greek yogurt + cream base vs cashew cream here).
